packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-19: UNVERIFIED IMAGE-ONLY READING

Exposure statement: Nothing in my context proposed an identification or reading of this item. The object itself carries a modern pencil shelfmark ("Stams, STA, Frg. 55r" on the written face, "Stams, STA, Frg. 55v" on the back) and a modern ink note on the back (transcribed below) giving a date and a former use; these are visible on the images, not prior context. I opened only PROMPT.md and image-001 to image-009 in this packet (I probed image-010 by path to find the end of the series; it does not exist). I listed no directory and consulted nothing else.

IMAGES
- image-001: reduced overview, written face (one horizontal strip of parchment, ~24-25 cm wide by scale).
- image-002 (left), image-003 (left-centre), image-004 (right-centre), image-005 (right): native tiles of the written face, overlapping horizontally.
- image-006: reduced overview, back face.
- image-007 (left), image-008 (centre), image-009 (right): native tiles of the back.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
- Landscape strip, single block of long lines running the full width; no columns, rubrics, initials or ruling seen. 15 full lines plus the tops of a 16th line at the bottom edge (cut). The first line begins mid-sentence ("zu ...burg Ritter"), so text above is lost; the strip is cut at top and bottom. Left and right edges look like the original margins (text starts near the left edge; right margin narrow).
- Script: German cursive (Kurrent-type) chancery hand, brown ink, with enlarged looped capitals at sentence/section starts (e.g. "Das", "Doch", "Vnnd", "Thatten", "Beschehen"); a long horizontal flourish-line after "brief /" (line 7) and before "Beschehen" (line 15) as line fillers.
- Folds: one horizontal fold across the middle and several vertical folds; a small slit at the centre fold. No damage that removes text except the cut edges.
- Back: blank except modern annotations (see end).
- Tentative interpretation (not inference of identity): a legal instrument in German in the first person ("wir", "mich selbs"), with sealing clause and dating clause at the end.

CONVENTIONS
Lines are numbered from the top of the written text (identical numbering on all four tiles, since each tile shows the full height). Each line is given as the stretches visible on each tile; overlaps between tiles are marked "(overlap)". Doubled consonants and "vnnd/vnd" kept as written as far as I can tell. "?" follows an uncertain reading; [illegible] where I could not read.
Note on strike-like strokes: this hand crosses capital E and some "tt/ff" with a horizontal bar; several words (see notes) look struck through, but I cannot always tell a deletion from the letter's own bar.

SELECTED AREAS / UNREAD
- I transcribed all 15 full lines of the written face. Weak points: proper names (L1 "Jaufenburg?", "Leonburg?"; L2 surname after "Cristoff" and final given name; L3 "Montany?", "Fried?"; L7 abbot's name), L8 toponyms ("Steg?", "ober Lana?"), L10 second half, L13 middle, and the day-numeral in L15.
- Line 16 (cut at bottom) is unreadable; any text above line 1 is lost.
- Some apparent strike-throughs (L4 "Edlen", L6 "Lehen"/"Erben", L12 word before "warr", L13 "Vrkhunde", L15 "tag") may be deletions or just this hand's barred capitals/flourishes; a raking-light or higher-magnification view would settle this.

LIMITATIONS
Unverified reading from images only. Expansions and spellings are as seen; uncertain forms carry "?". I did not supply words from expected formula wording; where formula-like phrases appear they are what I read on the tile.
